title: 🔎 Exa eval: R-1 nano and metadata routing at $0.25 to $1 per 10k pages
text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/41c4a78a1c8781009a33ece713086e73 as of 2026-11-19T01:45:15.408Z: {"Category":"exploration","Last edited":"2026-11-19T01:45:15.408Z","Name":"Exa eval: R-1 nano and metadata routing at \\$0.25 to \\$1 per 10k pages","Status":"Not started","date:Period:is_datetime":0,"date:Period:start":"2026-11-18","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/41c4a78a1c8781009a33ece713086e73"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🔎"} Ask: stamp this replay plan and its quality gate. Modeled, \$1 per 10k pages is reachable if Reducto hosts every page; \$0.25 only if Exa keeps routing in its stack. Quality on Exa's PDFs is unmeasured. All prices are illustrative, not quotes. ## Price model The [Parallel reference](https://apps.reducto.ai/internal/parallel-parse-options) prices R-1 nano first at \$1.04 per 10k pages. The [November 11 validation](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/8a7dc61e791349d193de8bc2888b730d) builds it from \$0.23 R-1 nano GPU, \$0.10 fallback and \$0.50 platform at 20% gross margin, with a 0.5% fallback rate from a public benchmark, not Exa's PDFs. Metadata routing reads the PDF's embedded text layer; trusted pages skip the models. The handoff is the share Exa sends to an outside parser, assumed 20% until Exa confirms. | Policy | Price per 10k pages | | --- | --- | | Exa routes in its stack, hands 20% to R-1 nano | \$0.21 Reducto charge, plus Exa's local cost | | Reducto hosts; metadata keeps 80%, R-1 nano takes 20% | \$0.83 to \$1.02, if metadata routing costs \$0.10 to \$0.25 | | Reducto hosts; R-1 nano on every page | \$1.04 | - \$1 hosted holds if metadata routing costs at most \$0.23 before margin. Platform alone sets a \$0.63 floor. - \$0.25 in Exa's stack leaves \$0.04 for Exa's extra local cost. - Fallback may run above 0.5%, since escalated pages are the hard ones. Price = (platform + metadata routing + each model + final fallback) / (1 − margin), charging every attempt and counting capacity, rendering, storage and egress once. ## Eval plan 1. Fix the replay set. 40,007 representative pages (30,003 index, 10,004 latest crawls) set price and quality; 10,000 hard cases report separately. Split by document, group near duplicates. Ask Exa for its routing mask, kept-page output and accept/reject criteria; without them, use a labeled 20% proxy and claim no parity. 2. Compare three setups on the same output (text, reading order, tables): - Exa today, the baseline. - Hosted: metadata routing, then R-1 nano, R-1 mini, R-1, approved final fallback. - Exa's stack: Exa routes locally and sends rejected pages to Reducto; measure local CPU and handoff latency. - Controls: metadata only, R-1 nano on every page, pinned R-1 as quality reference. Neither of the first two is a candidate: one has no fallback for bad text layers, the other costs \$1.04. 3. Pick the cheapest safe threshold. Log trust score, outcome, attempts and timings per page. Sweep on a calibration split from the 0.85 server default; lock before the held-out test. Missing scores and invalid output escalate, never drop. Judge with blind ParseBench diagnostics and pairwise preference against Exa's baseline; people check sampled disagreements. - Proposed gate: lower 95% bound on the serious-error-free rate difference no worse than −1 point vs Exa, with no material regression on index, latest or hard cases. 4. Check scale after quality passes. 20M pages/day is 231 pages/s hosted, 46 pages/s at a 20% handoff; if 20M is the handoff, 231 pages/s to Reducto and 1,157 hosted. Confirm which, then load test steady and peak. Approvals: R-1 nano has no API host on main ([registry](https://github.com/reductoai/api/blob/94173526fdd4627f2c436be197b285a436ce5df8/src/model_serving/registry/models/r1_nano.yaml#L1-L13)), so it runs on an approved internal eval runner. [Metadata routing](https://github.com/reductoai/api/blob/94173526fdd4627f2c436be197b285a436ce5df8/src/config/v3.py#L375-L377) is a US-only alpha; Platform must approve before Exa sees it. ## Results Graphs we expect to plot: | Graph | What it answers | | --- | --- | | Price vs quality: price per 10k pages vs serious-error-free rate, hosted and Exa's stack, with the \$0.25 to \$1 band, baseline, chosen threshold and 95% intervals | Which policy costs least at Exa's bar? | | Routing and misses: share per stage and failure by threshold, plus serious errors among pages metadata kept | How much stays cheap, and what does it miss? | | Cost breakdown: per-stage bars per 10k pages; Reducto charge vs Exa's total | Where does the money go as fallback rises? | | Throughput vs latency: pages/s vs p50/p95/p99 latency and errors, steady and peak | Does it keep up at Exa's volume? | After the replay: pick the cheapest threshold that passes the gate, then validate capacity before any quote. ## Impact - ParseJudge, 10k hard-case pages: metadata 4.7 vs 8.2 for R-1 nano; R-1 nano 7.7 vs 9.0 for R-1 mini.
